answers.how: A quadratic fit to the shark’s horizontal positions gives an initial speed of about 76 px/s and acceleration of about 38 px/s². The given acceleration therefore sets the scale to about 38 px/m.
The boat moves approximately 191 px/s. Dividing by the shark-derived scale of about 38 px/m gives its speed.
The fully visible boat is approximately 382 px long; dividing by about 38 px/m gives its length.
The shark is approximately 123 px long, corresponding to about 3.2 m at the acceleration-derived scale.
The shark’s top-to-bottom extent, including fins, is approximately 46 px. Dividing by about 38 px/m gives its height.
At 0.5 s, the estimated center-to-center separation is approximately 628 px. Converting with the acceleration-derived scale gives about 16.4 m.
